newsitem.title: HUNGARY: WHEAT, BARLEY FUTURES DROP IN SLOW BUDAPEST MARKET.
newsitem.headline: WHEAT, BARLEY FUTURES DROP IN SLOW BUDAPEST MARKET.

text.p: Most milling wheat futures ended lower and barley futures continued their plunge on the grain section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), traders said on Monday.
"Barley is still one of the most expensive feeds, so there are no buyers," said Robert Vajo of Termin.
Feed barley dropped 370 to 400 forints per tonne to end between 27,300 forints for April to 18,200 forints for October, except for March which remained unchanged at 26,560 forints.
Old (1996) crop milling wheat futures went down by the daily allowed 400 forints for March to end at 24,600 forints and dropped 320 forints for May to 22,930.
Poor export prospects and excess stocks were the main reason behind the price falls, Vajo said, adding that even mills are quietly selling wheat surplus.
New (1997) crop milling wheat futures finished mixed but prices only moved about 100 forints in either direction.
"Milling wheat prices are likely to hover around the 19,000 forints level until the end of March, when the first domestic and foreign crop forecasts are expected," Vajo said.
Maize futures remained steady except for the March maturity which closed at 17,900 forints, up 100.

Total turnover was a very modest 580 contracts or 220.96 million forints, which dealers attributed to their colleagues based outside Budapest being reluctant to trade on Monday. The BCE's grain section began trading on Monday at the beginning of this year.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
